name: Black-tipped Cotinga
rangeDescription: Humid lowlands of eastern panama to western colombia and northwestern ecuador
description: This stunning cotinga is found only from extreme eastern Panama to northwest Ecuador. Males are unmistakable in range: entirely snowy white with a reddish eye and tiny black spots on the wingtips and tail.

name: Puna Thistletail
rangeDescription: Andes of southern peru (southern cusco and puno)
description: Small brown bird with a very long, thin tail. Found in elfin forest and montane scrub around and above the treeline, where it forages singly or in pairs low in dense vegetation.

name: Jelski's Black-Tyrant
rangeDescription: East slope of andes from southeastern ecuador (zamora-chinchipe) southward to central peru (to junín)
description: Rare flycatcher found in cloud forest along the east slope of the Andes in northern and central Peru, barely reaching over the border into southeastern Ecuador. Male is dark sooty gray; female is grayish-olive with pale wingbars and faint streaking below.

name: Eastern Spot-billed Duck
rangeDescription: Breeds northeastern asia; winters to southern china, taiwan, and philippines
description: Common large duck of lakes, ponds, wet fields, and estuaries. Dark brown overall, with a pale head marked by a whitish eyebrow and two black stripes on the face.

name: White-winged Flufftail
rangeDescription: Highlands of ethiopia and eastern south africa
description: Very rare, small rail of montane marshes. Extremely shy and elusive bird that is unlikely to be seen unless expressly looking for it.

name: Rufous Crab Hawk
rangeDescription: Northeastern venezuela (río orinoco delta) to eastern brazil (paraná)
description: Large, chunky hawk of coastal forests, especially mangroves. Adult is mostly dark gray and rusty and is unmistakable in coastal habitat.

name: Gray-hooded Parakeet
rangeDescription: Andes of bolivia to northwestern argentina and northern chile
description: Small, gregarious parakeet of the high Andes from central Argentina to Lake Titicaca. Tends to forage in small groups in shorter shrubs and bushes, including Polylepis.

name: Madagascar Lark
rangeDescription: Grassland of madagascar
description: Small, streaky, brownish bird. Very common Madagascar endemic that is found in all open habitats; only absent from thick forest.

name: Brazilian Laniisoma
rangeDescription: Tropical southeastern brazil (espírito santo to eastern paraná)
description: A distinctive green-and-yellow species, slightly larger than a becard, with scaled sides and breast, a long hooked bill, and large eyes. Males have a black cap with olive-green cheeks and back and heavily scaled underparts.

name: Black-browed Barbet
rangeDescription: Montane forest of malay peninsula and sumatra
description: Loud but sluggish and difficult-to-see canopy inhabitant of highland forests in peninsular Malaysia and Sumatra. Note the leaf-green body, brightly colored face, and heavy black bill.

name: Blue-throated Macaw
rangeDescription: Northern bolivia (llanos de moxos, beni)
description: Large macaw endemic to flooded grasslands of El Beni, Bolivia (Llanos de Moxos). Breeds in cavities in tall palms, and threatened by habitat loss.

name: Herald Petrel
rangeDescription: Breeds in the tropical pacific ocean (raine island, tonga, and french polynesia to easter island); pelagic range incompletely known, but occurs regularly to the central pacific ocean
description: Medium-sized, lightly built petrel of offshore tropical waters across the Pacific; not seen from mainland. Plumage is highly variable (from white-bodied and dark-headed to wholly dark) and often very similar to larger and broader-winged Kermadec Petrel, which has a shorter and broader tail than Herald.

name: Steller's Eider
rangeDescription: Northwestern and northeastern siberia from yamal peninsula to chukotka; and arctic coastal plain, northern alaska; winters to kamchatka peninsula, commander and kuril islands (southeastern russia), and aleutian islands; also kola peninsula, barents and white seas (northwestern russia), and baltic sea
description: Unique Arctic sea duck. Much smaller than other eiders (and in a different genus); only slightly larger than Harlequin Duck.

name: Dusky Pigeon
rangeDescription: Lowland rainforest of western colombia to northwestern ecuador
description: This pigeon is found in the Choco region of western Colombia and Ecuador. It is fairly dull grayish-brown overall, especially gray on the head and breast with a warmer reddish tone on the nape.

name: Socotra Buzzard
rangeDescription: Socotra (off eastern somalia)
description: A typical medium-sized brown-and-white buzzard that was only recognized as distinct in 2010. The underparts are whitish buff with heavily streaked underparts (lighter on the throat).

name: Peruvian Pigeon
rangeDescription: Northern peru (subtropical marañón valley) and adjacent southern ecuador
description: Large, rusty pigeon confined to the Marañon drainage of northwestern Peru. Its range may extend to extreme southern Ecuador, but evidence is lacking.

name: Gray-backed Tachuri
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (central bahia to minas gerais and northern são paulo)
description: A small rare and endemic flycatcher with a conspicuous white patch in front of the eyes and a short white eyebrow. Also note its gray crown and a brownish-gray back and cinnamon washed breast and sides.

name: Cinnamon-tailed Fantail
rangeDescription: Tanimbar islands (larat, yamdena, lutu, mutu, and selaru) and babar
description: A distinctive songbird with a long tail, often cocked to expose the diagnostic cinnamon sides. Also note the gray back, cinnamon flash in the wing, and buff belly.

name: Black-faced Munia
rangeDescription: Lowlands of wallacea (except for lesser sundas)
description: A striking finch with a black hood, light brown collar, extensively barred white underside, and pale barred rump. Juveniles duller, brown above and buffy below, lacking bars.

name: Pied Wheatear
rangeDescription: Stony south-central eurasia; winters to arabia, iran, and northeastern africa
description: Jaunty little terrestrial songbird of plains, agricultural fields, and semi-desert, where often perches prominently on utility wires and boulders. Tuxedoed breeding male is black with snow-white crown, belly, and rump.
